description: Paper-reported metrics plus reproduction-status metadata for selected method families. Used by generate_paper_comparison.py and generate_reproduction_status.py. Schema v3 introduces the `claim_level` field, which classifies each entry against the localization_zoo reproduction taxonomy (reproduced / approximately_reproduced / indicative / smoke / ported).

claim_level_definitions.reproduced: Same dataset variant, same sequence, same evaluation protocol, same sensor condition as the source paper, ideally full sequence, with metric values consistent with the paper or official leaderboard.
claim_level_definitions.approximately_reproduced: Dataset family matches but window / preprocessing / metric implementation / parameters diverge in a way that prevents one-to-one comparison. Useful for directional comparison.
claim_level_definitions.indicative: Short window, Raw-vs-Odometry mismatch, custom window, or no direct paper claim to match. Useful inside the repo benchmark, not a paper-result reproduction.
claim_level_definitions.smoke: Demonstrates that the contract works end-to-end. Not for accuracy comparison.
claim_level_definitions.ported: Inputs and outputs are wired up but no paper-comparable benchmark is targeted (e.g. concept-only baselines, custom integrations).

litamin2.paper: Yokozuka et al., LiTAMIN2: Ultra Light LiDAR-based SLAM using Geometric Approximation Applied with KL-Divergence, ICRA 2021
litamin2.repo_scope_label: Paper-oriented front-end reimplementation with the paper odometry pipeline
litamin2.repo_scope_summary: The repo reproduces the LiTAMIN2 registration front-end and also keeps a paper-like 3 m profile inside the shared benchmark harness.
litamin2.reproduction_status_label: Near paper across KITTI Odometry 00-10 (paper pipeline, no GT seed)
litamin2.reproduction_status_summary: --litamin2-paper-odometry follows Sec. III of the paper: raw scans voted into 3 m normal distributions, a voxel map of distributions, nearest-distribution pairing, and the ICP+Cov cost (shape term linear in the cost, Newton steps). Run unchanged on all 11 sequences it scores official KITTI RTE 1.01/2.06/1.15/0.76/0.90/0.62/0.58/0.48/0.98/0.78/0.99 % on 00-10 versus the paper's ICP+Cov row 0.78/2.10/0.95/0.96/1.05/0.55/0.55/0.48/1.01/0.69/0.80 % (Table III, no loop closure): geometric mean 1.05x. The ICP-only variant against the same map gives 1.01x versus the paper's ICP row. Table 6 picks the best variant per sequence and reaches 1.00x.
litamin2.numeric_comparison_label: Same metric, ~1.05x with one fixed setting on 00-10
litamin2.numeric_comparison_summary: Official KITTI RTE of paper_icp_cov (one setting, all sequences) vs the paper's ICP+Cov row: 00 1.009 vs 0.78, 01 2.062 vs 2.10, 02 1.148 vs 0.95, 03 0.756 vs 0.96, 04 0.902 vs 1.05, 05 0.624 vs 0.55, 06 0.578 vs 0.55, 07 0.477 vs 0.48, 08 0.984 vs 1.01, 09 0.777 vs 0.69, 10 0.986 vs 0.80; geometric mean 1.05x. paper_icp_first (ICP term only) vs the paper's ICP row: 1.01x. The earlier harness path (0.5 m pre-downsampling, at most 2500 source points, a point map rebuilt into voxels, same-voxel pairing) stayed at 1.22x on 00/02/05/07/08. Table 6 (docs/assets/paper/paper_ratio_table.csv) selects the best 100 m RPE variant per sequence; see papers/litamin2/README.md.
litamin2.main_blocker: None for the KITTI numbers. The shape term only helps when the map holds single-scan distributions (the first one per voxel); against aggregated map voxels it hurts (2.0x, diverges on 04 and 08), which the paper does not discuss. Loop closure is not implemented.
litamin2.next_step: Loop closure (Table III rows with loop closure) is out of scope; the paper odometry could become the method default once other datasets are checked.
litamin2.reported_hardware: Intel Core i9-9900K, 32 GB RAM, NVIDIA GPU (Sec. IV)
litamin2.notes: Paper values were re-verified against the arXiv PDF on 2026-10-03 (Table III, ICP+Cov without loop closure; the ICP-only row is 0.75/1.88/0.99/0.84/0.90/0.74/0.45/0.55/1.25/0.74/1.36 %). Results: experiments/results/litamin2_kitti_seq_NN_full_paper_matrix.json. The older harness-path sweeps (voxel resolution, correspondence radius and gate, covariance floor, covariance gradient, coarse-to-fine) remain in the other litamin2 aggregates; they used GT-free constant-velocity seeds but not the paper's map or input. Policy A GT-seeded numbers (0.74 % on Raw 0009 short window, 1.26 % on MulRan parkinglot full) remain non-comparable to the paper.

gicp.reproduction_status_summary: The implementation is useful as benchmark evidence for the GICP idea, but not as a paper-result reproduction of a specific historical codebase.
gicp.numeric_comparison_summary: The original paper predates the repo's modern public benchmark suite and does not provide a standardized numeric target that can be matched one-to-one here.
gicp.main_blocker: There is no single paper benchmark and hardware protocol to reproduce against.
gicp.next_step: Choose a concrete upstream GICP benchmark target, or keep GICP explicitly scoped as conceptual baseline evidence.
gicp.notes: Original GICP paper predates KITTI. No standardized numeric benchmark reported. Comparison is with the concept, not specific numbers. As supporting evidence under the dogfooding-fixed --no-gt-seed pure-odometry path (build 2026-05-18, velocity-model prior), GICP fast on KITTI Raw 0009 full reports ATE 4.82 m / RPE 4.70 % (best in the Policy A family on this sequence, edging LiTAMIN2's 7.45 m). This is honest pure-odometry behavior but not a paper-reproduction claim; it is an internal calibration of where GICP sits versus other Policy A methods when the GT-seed asymmetry is removed.

kiss_icp.paper: Vizzo et al., KISS-ICP: In Defense of Point-to-Point ICP, RAL 2023
kiss_icp.repo_scope_summary: The repo keeps a small KISS-ICP-style local-map pipeline that preserves the main idea while simplifying the full upstream engineering stack.
kiss_icp.reproduction_status_label: Matches the official code on KITTI 00/07 with upstream mechanics
kiss_icp.reproduction_status_summary: With --kiss-upstream-profile --kiss-model-deviation-threshold --kiss-geman-mcclure-kernel --kiss-map-min-point-distance 0.2236068 and the KITTI elevation correction the port scores 0.535 % (seq 00) and 0.363 % (seq 07) official KITTI RTE against 0.528 % and 0.375 % for the official KISS-ICP 1.3.0 code. The repository default keeps a simpler speed-based adaptive threshold and is not a faithful rerun.
kiss_icp.numeric_comparison_label: KITTI 00/04 per sequence plus the 00-10 average
kiss_icp.numeric_comparison_summary: The paper reports per-sequence KITTI RTE only for seq 00 (0.51 %) and 04 (0.36 %), plus the 00-10 average (0.50 %). Upstream KISS-ICP corrects the KITTI elevation angle by +0.205 deg in its KITTI loader. With the same correction and the upstream mechanics (model-deviation threshold, Geman-McClure kernel, map insertion gate) the port scores 0.535 % on seq 00 (1.05x) and 0.373 % on seq 04 (1.04x), and 0.564 % pooled over 00-10, identical to the official KISS-ICP 1.3.0 code on the same pipeline (0.564 %, 1.13x the paper's average). Before matching the adaptive threshold the best seq 00 value was 0.708 % (1.39x), and 0.954 % on raw scans (1.87x). Seq 00/04 values are the best variant among the sweeps on that sequence (selected on the evaluated sequence, so optimistic); see docs/kitti_elevation_correction.md, papers/kiss_icp/README.md, and docs/assets/paper/paper_ratio_table.csv (Table 6).
kiss_icp.main_blocker: The remaining 1.13x on the 00-10 average is shared by the official 1.3.0 code, so it lies between the paper and the released code (for example an older release or a different deskewing setup), not in the port.
kiss_icp.next_step: Optionally rerun an older official KISS-ICP release on 00-10 to locate the paper-vs-release difference; the port itself needs no further change for KITTI.
kiss_icp.notes: KISS-ICP reports the KITTI average relative translational error (Table II: 0.50 % train / 0.61 % test) and per-sequence values only in the Table VI threshold ablation. The paper does not state hardware or a KITTI frame rate.

ct_icp.paper: Dellenbach et al., CT-ICP: Real-time Elastic LiDAR Odometry with Loop Closure, ICRA 2022
ct_icp.repo_scope_label: Paper-oriented core reimplementation with an upstream-mechanics pipeline
ct_icp.repo_scope_summary: The repo implements the continuous-time two-pose-per-scan core, interpolation, and point-to-plane optimization described by CT-ICP. --ct-icp-upstream-mechanics runs a dedicated pipeline that follows upstream jedeschaud/ct_icp with its driving profile (papers/ct_icp/README.md).
ct_icp.reproduction_status_label: Matches the official code on KITTI 00-10 with upstream mechanics
ct_icp.reproduction_status_summary: With --ct-icp-upstream-mechanics and the KITTI elevation correction the port scores 0.587 % official KITTI RTE pooled over sequences 00-10 against 0.585 % for the official jedeschaud/ct_icp code on the same scans (run_official_ct_icp_baseline.py), and stays within 0.05 points of it on every sequence (seq 07: 0.315 % vs 0.308 %, paper 0.31 %). The default runCTICP pipeline is not a faithful rerun: it used the point index as time, a 20-frame window and zero-motion initialisation, scored 1.03-1.18 % on seq 07, and is numerically unstable (about +/-7-11 % under 1e-6 deg input perturbations), which explains the earlier host dependence.
ct_icp.numeric_comparison_summary: Official KITTI RTE on KITTI-corrected scans, port with --ct-icp-upstream-mechanics vs paper Table I: 00 0.525/0.49, 01 0.716/0.76, 02 0.549/0.52, 03 0.586/0.72, 04 0.717/0.39, 05 0.315/0.25, 06 0.284/0.27, 07 0.315/0.31, 08 0.902/0.81, 09 0.629/0.49, 10 0.742/0.48; pooled 00-10 0.587 % vs 0.531 % (the paper's per-sequence values weighted by segment count), 1.10x. The official code gives 0.585 % pooled on the same scans, so the remaining difference lies between the paper and the released code. Before the upstream mechanics the best of ~313 sweep variants was 4.03x (geometric mean over 00/02/05/07/08). See papers/ct_icp/README.md and docs/assets/paper/paper_ratio_table.csv (Table 6).
ct_icp.main_blocker: The remaining 1.10x on the 00-10 average (largest on 04/05/09/10) is shared by the official code on the same scans, so it lies between the paper and the released code (for example the paper's KITTI PLY timestamps or an older release), not in the port.
ct_icp.next_step: Optionally obtain the official KITTI PLY files (password-protected download) to check whether their per-point timestamps explain the paper-vs-release difference; the port itself needs no further change for KITTI.
ct_icp.notes: Paper values were re-verified against the arXiv PDF on 2026-10-03. Repo values are the official KITTI RTE (100-800 m) from re-running, with the current code, the variant with the best 100 m RPE in the full non-GT-seeded sweep for that sequence (experiments/results/kitti_rte_rescore.json); selection on the evaluated sequence makes them optimistic. See docs/assets/paper/paper_ratio_table.csv (Table 6). The --ct-icp-gt-seed toggle remains available for fair-prior dogfooding-style cross-method comparison; GT-seeded rows are excluded from Table 6.
